Two intervals, two different questions

What sits outside both intervals?

  • Age-group versus pro race conditions
  • Different courses and distances
  • Who enters the ranked comparison group
  • Whether the season assumptions hold

These are exploratory model-based intervals. They are not a 95% probability statement about your true world rank.

The provisional world estimate

How the statistics are calculated
  1. Match athlete names after removing punctuation and accents and ignoring case. Exclude ambiguous duplicate names from modelling. Preserve the source ranking tables unchanged.
  2. For PTO race performance, use the mean of positive results in each athlete’s displayed scoring breakdown. Zero-point rows remain in the evidence. This estimates a successful-scoring-finishes scenario, rather than the risk of DNFs or an incomplete season.
  3. Fit either ordinary least squares or Huber robust regression. Robust regression reduces the influence of large residuals; it does not resolve differences between the ranking systems.
  4. For each configuration, resample athletes with replacement 1,000 times and refit the model. The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles give an exploratory 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the fitted mean.
  5. For the prediction distribution, add a sampled, centred, leverage-adjusted residual to each bootstrap fitted value. This adds between-athlete scatter. It assumes this scatter is applicable at my score and does not shrink by the square root of four races.
  6. For PTO performance, multiply each race-score draw by the chosen scoring-finish count, divide by four, then count how many entries in the saved PTO table have more points. Other athletes stay fixed. Ties require official rules.
  7. For published-rank models, fit rank directly and round the draws to whole positions. Display ranks below 1 at 1 and beyond the last listed athlete as “N+”. Boundary mass is reported. This is a snapshot comparison, not a full-season ability estimate.
  8. The confidence band is for the fitted mean only. Cohort and method selection are not included in any one interval. Compare the alternatives to see that sensitivity. Intervals are exploratory, rely on exchangeability and residual assumptions, and are not validated coverage guarantees.

MyTriRanking “overall” and “best” use the matching score column for every athlete. The nearby group always means overall MyTriRanking score below 900. The complete-results group means four positive displayed PTO scores. Leave-one-out error refits without each athlete in turn.

Each configuration uses a fixed random seed for reproducibility. Confidence and prediction intervals use the percentile method. The distribution bars show the share of simulated draws in a rank bin, not an empirically validated probability of my real rank.

R documentation: confidence and prediction intervals · Huber robust regression in MASS

Data coverage and sources

This HTML is a frozen, offline snapshot. Main ranking data were retrieved on 25 November 2026. The PTO and OpenRank tables are dated 23 November 2026 where update dates are supplied.

  • MyTriRanking: British women’s middle-distance top 1,000, including my overall score of 836.95, best score of 840.76 and British rank of 88.
  • PTO World Rankings: 473 published ranked entries plus verified scoring breakdowns for 38 matched athletes. The two Rachel Brown entries are retained in the ranking threshold table. MyTriRanking also contains two distinct Rachel Brown athlete IDs, so that ambiguous name is excluded from both systems’ models.
  • ProTriNews OpenRank: 460 ranked women and 38 unambiguous matches. The full export does not include points and scoring-race counts. The separate top-100 points file is insufficient for an adjusted estimate near my level.
  • PTO methodology · OpenRank methodology. Their scores are not interchangeable.

There is no claim here to an official rank or pro eligibility. The target is a position within the selected ranking’s current listed field, not all female triathletes worldwide. Same-course, same-day comparisons would strengthen the analysis. A year-end comparison requires matching historical performance data and scoring rules.

Re-knit this dashboard in RStudio

Open sofya-world-ranking-2026-11-25.Rmd and click Knit. Keep analysis.R, dashboard.html and the data folder alongside it. The data_dir parameter points to the blog folder containing the ranking CSVs. Refresh the scoring evidence when changing the PTO snapshot; the source stops if the scores do not reconcile.

The R source computes all 28 supported model configurations and their bootstrap draws. The HTML then switches between those results locally, without a server or internet connection. Packages: rmarkdown, knitr, MASS and jsonlite.
